entities.name: Breast cancer
observations: Human tumor studies evaluated HPV, phosphorylated STAT3, and IL-17 expression in breast cancer.
HPV detection prevalence and associations vary substantially across cohorts and assays.

entities.name: Human papillomavirus
observations: HPV16/18 was detected in 34 of 325 breast-cancer specimens (10.5%) in a 379-patient study and was associated with high p-STAT3 and IL-17 immunostaining.
A separate case-control study detected HPV DNA in 35 of 72 breast-cancer specimens (48.6%) and reported increased IL-17 and inflammatory mediators in HPV-positive cancers.

entities.name: Phosphorylated STAT3
observations: In the 2016 breast-cancer cohort, high p-STAT3 immunostaining occurred in 146 of 379 tumors (38.5%) and was associated with HPV positivity (P=0.018).
Independent breast-tumor cohorts show context-dependent prognostic associations for nuclear pSTAT3, including improved survival in some node-negative and node-positive cohorts.

entities.name: IL-17
observations: In the 2016 breast-cancer cohort, high IL-17 immunostaining occurred in 233 of 379 tumors (61.5%) and was associated with HPV positivity (P=0.021).
Separate human breast-tumor studies indicate that IL-17 staining can primarily reflect peritumoral macrophage-like or infiltrating immune cells rather than malignant epithelial cells.

entities.name: PMID:27508043
observations: A 379-patient breast-cancer study used GenChip HPV detection and immunohistochemistry for p-STAT3 and IL-17; HPV positivity was significantly associated with both markers, but reported abstract data lacked effect sizes and did not establish causality.

entities.name: PMID:30642295
observations: A breast-cancer case-control study reported HPV DNA and increased IL-17 and inflammatory mediators in HPV-positive cancers but did not measure STAT3/pSTAT3.
